result.summary: The landlord clearly approved an engineer visit ("Yes please arrange an engineer, thank you", event 008). I recorded the approval, moved the ticket to provider selection and emailed the tenant that the landlord has agreed. I did not assign a contractor because there is no appliance engineer on record. There is also an identical ticket, R/PM042-2, for the same job, so two contractors could be sent. I've passed both to ops at normal priority and put the ticket on hold with a 1-day follow-up.
result.situation: Tenant reported that the washing machine doesn't heat water on 60°C+ cycles. The agency asked the landlord by email whether to send its usual appliance engineer, and the landlord replied yes. A system note asked whether the landlord needs a reply.

judgement.why_this_decision: The landlord's reply was an unconditional approval of the visit (classifier: approval probability 0.91, routine). Following lessons #41 and #49, I recorded it, sent no further reply to the landlord and moved to provider selection. The landlord was asked to approve 'our appliance engineer', but the records don't name that engineer. find_contractors only found boiler firms (matched on the wrong 'Heating & Hot Water' category) or firms matched on name alone, with no record of appliance work or past jobs at this property. Ticket 98 (R/PM042-2) is at the same address with the same job reference, NBL-042, and identical messages, so assigning here could double-dispatch. The guidance says to escalate when nobody suitable exists, so I did.

alternatives_considered.option: Assign Calder Heating or Harlow Heating
alternatives_considered.why_not: They are heating/boiler firms that only matched because the job is filed under the wrong category. There is no evidence they repair appliances.
They matched on name only. There is no history of them working at this property or in this trade, and the duplicate ticket raises the risk of sending two contractors.
The approval was clear. Lessons #41 and #49 say no reply is needed.
